Mr Md Imam Respondent No. 2. Hasan, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Internationl Tannery & another ----- Petitioners
 Vs
Judge, Artha Rin Adalat at No. 4 ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
JBM Hassan J: In this Rule Nisi, the petitioners have challenged entertainment of the Artha jari Case No. 170 of 2007 and continuation thereof before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka arises out of the judgment and decree dated 12-5-2003 (decree draw on 31-8-2003) passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 432 of 1996 decreeing Title Suit No. 106 of 1993 for Taka 3,57,46,721.78 with simple interest @ 14% till realization of the decretal amount. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying plaintiff's claim. Ultimately, the Adalat by judgment and decree dated 12-10-1996 decreed the suit in part for Taka 1,10,00,000 and accordingly preliminary decree was drawn up on 19-10-1996. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiff Bank preferred First Appeal No. 432 of 1996 before the High Court Division. After hearing, the appeal has been allowed by judgment and decree dated 12-5-2003 (decree drawn up on 31-8-2003) for Taka 3,57,46,721.78 with simple interest @ 14% with a direction that the decretal dues be paid within 12 months failing which the decree shall be made final and the plaintiff Bank shall be able to realize the dues by selling out the mortgaged property through execution case. 

 4. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree the petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1287 of 2003 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division and after hearing, it was dismissed by judgment and Order dated 24-5-2007 affirming the judgment and decree of the High Court Division. 

 5. Thereafter, on 2-8-2007 the decree holder Bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 170 of 2007 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka (the Adalat) to execute the aforementioned decree impleading the petitioners as judgment-debtors. The petitioners on 11-10-2007 filed an application before the executing Court praying for rejecting the execution case on the ground that there being no final decree as per judgment of the Court, the execution case cannot proceed. The said application was rejected on 30-3-2008. On the other hand, the decree holder Bank also filed an application in the original suit (Annexure-G to the writ petition) on 19-2-2008 before the Adalat praying to draw up a final decree and another application was also filed to get back the original documents (Exhibits) and that both the applications are still pending and till now no final decree has been drawn up. In the circumstances, the petitioners again filed an application on 20-4-2008 praying to dismiss the Artha Jari Case on the ground that there is no final decree as per judgment of the High Court Division and, as such, the execution case is premature. 

 6. In the meantime, the Adalat had been proceeding with the execution case and fixed the case on 26-4-2008 for selling the mortgaged property in auction. On the day of auction, no bidder having been found in the auction process, the decree holder Bank made a prayer for issuing title certificate under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (shortly, the Ain, 2003). In this backdrop, the petitioners have challenged entertainment of the execution case and continuation thereof, by filing writ petition before this Court under its constitutional jurisdiction, obtained the present Rule and interim Order of stay. 

 7. The Bank as the respondent No. 2 has been contesting the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements as made in the writ petition. This respondent also contends that section 5 (4) of the Ain, 2003 provides that except the decree of foreclosure suit, the other decrees passed by the Artha Rin Adalat become final with the sale of mortgaged property. The present suit is not a foreclosure suit. It is a suit for recovery of the bank loan by selling the mortgaged property and, as such, no final decree is required as per section 5 (4) of the Ain, 2003. Therefore, the Rule does not have any merit and, as such, it is liable to be discharged. 

 8. Mr AKM Asiful Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners after placing the writ petition and all its annexures, submits that the High Court Division passed the judgment and decree in the preliminary form with a direction that on failure to make the payment within 12 months, the decree shall be made final to realize the decretal dues by selling the mortgaged property in execution case and the said judgment has been affirmed by the Appellate Division. But the decree holder Bank without having any final decree as per requirement of the aforesaid judgment and decree, put the decree into execution. Therefore, the execution case on the face of it premature and cannot proceed. He further submits that though the prevailing law is that all the Artha decrees, except the decree of foreclosure suit, do not require to be made final decree for execution but in this particular case the Court has specifically required final decree for execution. Therefore, the present execution case cannot proceed without final decree and thus, the execution case on the face of it premature for want of final decree. In view of the facts, the Artha jari case should be interfered by this Court under its constitutional jurisdiction. 

 9. In reply to the aforesaid submissions, Mr Md Imam Hasan, the learned Advocate, appearing for the respondent No. 2 submits that the judgment and decree was passed on 12-5-2003 and that on 1st May, 2003 the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 introduced the provision that except the foreclosure suit in the case of simple Artha decree, no final decree is required and on the basis of the preliminary decree, the execution case will be proceeded and the preliminary decree would be final after selling the mortgaged property. In view of prevailing legal position, the decree holder Bank does not required any final decree to execute the preliminary decree of the Artha Rin Suit and, as such, the Adalat is proceeding rightly with the execution case having the sanction of law. He further submits that just 11 days before the Judgment, the law was enacted expressing provision that no final decree is required and that the latest legal position (as amended on 1-5-2003) having not been brought to the notice of the High Court Division, the preliminary decree was passed on 12-5-2003 requiring final decree. Thus, the decision of the High Court Division being per-incuriam, the executing Court is not bound to follow the same in proceeding with the execution case by the final decree. In this regard, the learned Advocate refers to the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs Gurnam Kaur reported in AIR 1989 (SC) 38. 

 11. It appears that the execution case has been initiated to execute the judgment and decree dated 12-5-2003 (preliminary decree drawn up on 31-8-2003) passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 432 of 1996 decreeing the Title Suit No. 106 of 1993 for Taka 3,57,46,721.78 under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Relevant ordering portion of the said judgment runs as follows:— 

 "And it is further ordered and decreed that the plaintiff Bank is hereby entitled to get Taka 3,57,46,721.78 from the defendant together with 14% simple interest thereon per annum to be calculated from the date of filing of the suit till realization of the decretal amount with 12(twelve) months  failing which, the decree shall be made final and the plaintiff Bank shall be able to  realize the dues by selling out the mortgaged property through execution case." 

 12. Ultimately the aforesaid judgment and decree has been affirmed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division by the judgment and Order dated 24-5-2007 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1287 of 2003. 

 13. On the basis of the aforesaid judgment and decree, the decree holder Bank has filed an application for drawing up final decree. But the said final decree has not yet been drawn up as it is evidenced from the Annexure-G(2) to the writ petition. 

 14. In view of the facts, the question now arises as whether the executing Court can entertain the execution case to execute a preliminary decree as per the judgment and preliminary decree of the Court and wherein no final decree has yet been drawn up. 

 15. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force on 1-5-2003 providing the provisions exempting to make final decree for execution of the Artha decree except the decree passed in foreclosure suit. In order to appreciate the legal position, the relevant provisions are quoted herein below:— 

 (৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এর অধীন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক দায়েরকৃত মামলা নিষ্ক্রিয় সমাপ্তির (Forcelosure) উদ্দেশ্যে একটি বন্ধকী মামলা (Mortgage suit) হইলে, কেবলমাত্র সেইক্ষেত্রে আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রি প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি হইবে (Preliminary decree) এবং অন্যান্য সকল ক্ষেত্রে ঋণ অনাদায়ার্থে দায়েরকৃত মামলায় আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রি চুড়ান্ত ডিক্রি হইবে। 

 16. On the basis of the aforesaid legal pro-vision, the question earlier arose as to whether final decree is required to execute the Artha Rin decree which was filed for realization of loan money by selling the mortgaged property. In this context law has already been settled by the High Court Division as well as our Apex Court deciding that except the decrees passed in mortgage suits for foreclosure, the decrees passed in other mortgage suits do not require to be made final for the purpose of starting the execution case. In this regard in the case of KM Mozahid Islam vs Bangladesh reported in VI ADC (2009) 865 their Lordships held as under:— 

 "It appears from the prayer portion, quoted above, that the 'respondent bank has prayed for personal decree in preliminary form and further prayed for sale of the mortgaged property in case of default of the part of the judgment debtor in satisfying the decree, to be passed. Thus the suit as framed and filed cannot be said to attract section- 5(3) of the Ain but the same attracts section 5(4) of the Air, and therefore a decree passed in preliminary form after sale of the mortgage property automatically becomes a final decree. Thus we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Advocate that the decree, being passed in preliminary form, cannot be put into execution for realization of decreetal amount by sale of the mortgage property, before making the decree final, and hence the decree is bad in the eye of law." 

 17. Besides the aforesaid decision, in a good number of cases the High Court Division including this Bench also held that except mortgage the decree of foreclosure suit the other Artha decrees do no required any final decree though it is obtained for realization of loan money by selling the mortgaged property. 

 18. In view of aforesaid established principle that final decree is not required to execute the Artha decree, the question now arises whether in this particular case in our hand, the Adalat can proceed to execute the decree of the High Court Division passed in the form of preliminary decree. 

 19. It appears that in this case, the Adalat (executing Court) is proceeding the execute a particular judgment and decree. Therefore, the executing Court (Adalat) has to be remained confined within the periphery of this particular judgment and decree and that operating portion of the judgment and decree are as follows:— 

 "And it is further ordered and decreed that the plaintiff Bank is hereby entitled to get Taka 3,57,46,721.78 from the defendant together with 14% simple interest thereon per annum to be calculated from the date of filing of the suit till realization of the decretal amount with 12(twelve) months failing which, the decree shall be made  final and the plaintiff Bank shall be able to  realize the dues by selling out the  mortgaged property through execution Case." 

 20. Though legal position is that Artha decree except foreclosure suits, does not require final decree for execution case but since the present judgment itself requires final decree before execution. Therefore, the executing Court must have final decree for execution of the decree and, as such, without final decree, the execution case appears to us premature. In view of the above, the Adalat cannot entertain any execution case to execute the aforesaid decree in the preliminary form requiring final decree and, as such, continuation of the said execution case is unlawful apparent on the face of record without having any legal sanction. 

 22. But the case before us appears that the judgment itself has required a final decree and, as such, the executing Court cannot proceed to execute the said decree unless the decree is made final. The Adalat is, therefore, bound to draw up final decree as per requirement of the judgment of the High Court Division. As such, the cited decision is not applicable in the case before us in view of its different facts and circumstances. 

 23. In view of above discussions, we are led to held that since the very judgment requires final decree, without such final decree the executing Court cannot entertain any execution proceeding. Therefore, the Adalat is proceeding with a premature decree without having any legal sanction and, as such, the proceeding of the Artha Jari Case is liable to be interfered. Thus, we find merit in this Rule. 

 25. Since it is evident that the decree-holder Bank has already filed an application praying to draw up final decree and it is now pending before the Adalat, the decree holder bank is at liberty to file a fresh execution case after obtaining the final decree.
